Jumping game: Show how to jump with both feet together. Try a few times on the mat, holding their hand.
Put red balls in the red bucket and blue ones in the blue bucket. Fix the mixed-up ones together.
Roll the dough into snakes and balls. Show how to press with cutters; remind them not to put it in their mouth.
Describe what you do during the day: “We're putting on socks.” Then ask the child “What are we doing?”.
Set up a three-step course such as crawl under, jump over, go around. Say the order together.
Line the containers up from biggest to smallest. Mix them up and let the child order them.
Prepare paper and an apron. Let them make marks with their hands and mix colours; then clean up together.
Act out short scenes where the puppet is sad, angry or happy. Ask the child “How does the puppet feel?”.
Show how to cut paper strips with round-tipped child scissors. Teach carrying scissors with the tip pointing down.
Roll the dice and add a sentence to the story using the picture. Take turns.
Build a pattern such as red-blue-red-blue. Ask the child to find the next colour.
Take the roles of cashier and customer. Practise counting and saying thank you within the game.
Stand on one foot together and count to 5. Switch feet; if they wobble, laugh and try again.
Look for the first letter of the child's name in writing around the house. When you find it, say its sound together.
First guess, then put the object in the water and see. Sort the results into two groups. Never leave the water unattended.
Play a short game that teaches waiting your turn and accepting losing. Go over the rules together before playing.
Wearing a helmet, practise on flat ground away from traffic. Start with short distances.
Let the child cut fruit with a butter knife and mix it into yoghurt. Start with handwashing.
Observe the weather each day and draw a sun, cloud or rain on the chart. Count at the end of the week.
Make an illustrated “letter” for a grandparent or friend. The child tells, you write; they try writing their own name.
